axes.model_access: The main line is Alibaba's Tongyi Qianwen (Qwen) series — the Qwen official blog (qwenlm.github.io/blog) has a model-release line, and the open-weight line (HF/ModelScope) and the cloud chat are the same family. In-app model tiers are per the signed-in UI; Alibaba Cloud Model Studio (Bailian) is the developer API line, another interface from the same vendor.
axes.runtime: Web (tongyi.aliyun.com) + iOS/Android apps + PC client; generation is processed on Alibaba's cloud, no model runs locally. The Tongyi product line also has adjacent products like Tongyi Wanxiang (image/video generation) — don't mix them into this dossier.
axes.local_files: Chat history is stored on the account side; document/image parsing happens in the cloud. No locally-oriented data surface declared by the official side.
axes.background: Chats return instantly; "efficiency/deep thinking"-type modes are in-session tier switches; no official statement verified for an async task-queue form.
axes.tools: In-product capability lines incl. document parsing, image understanding and web retrieval (seen in the official-site navigation); agent/browser-extension entries exist, details not verified item by item. No official statement verified for MCP support.
axes.context: Session history syncs across devices when signed in; no official statement verified for a cross-session memory mechanism (if unknown, say unknown).
axes.permissions: Account system (Alipay/Alibaba/phone-number login); the training-use switch path not verified item by item. The Qwen model filing number is in the cn block (cross-verified against official public disclosures).
axes.fit: Suits: Chinese Q&A + multimodal understanding, wanting the Qwen open-weight same family (cloud and local both options), connecting with the Alibaba Cloud ecosystem (Model Studio API). Does not suit: office/social ecosystem integration (the DingTalk line is another product surface), or fully leaving the account system.
